# 2026-07-26 · Settlement currency

Change ID: `settlement-currency`
Created: `2026-07-26T13:38:43+00:00`
Risk: R2
Status: In progress

## Problem and intended outcome

Two partners onboarding this quarter settle in currencies other than USD.
Today the currency is implied by the partner and hard-coded at the reporting
layer, which is already wrong for one existing partner and is being worked
around by hand each month.

The intended outcome is that the settlement currency is stored on the order
itself, so the adapter can send it with the payload and reporting can read it
from the row instead of a lookup table.

## Success and non-goals

Success is that reporting derives currency from the order row for every
order, with historic rows backfilled to USD (correct for every order placed
so far).

Not in scope: a per-partner currency table (see decision below), and any
change to how amounts themselves are stored or rounded — that is tracked
separately under `partner-settlement-rounding`.

## Existing responsibilities searched

`src/db/schema.py` owns the stored order columns and now includes
`settlement_currency` (uncommitted). `src/api/partner_adapter.py` owns the
settlement payload shape and will own including the currency in that payload.
The reporting read path is not yet present in this repository.

## System and data flow

Order row (`settlement_currency` column) -> `to_partner_payload` -> partner
settlement API, and Order row -> reporting read path (reads currency from the
row instead of a per-partner lookup).

## Decisions and trade-offs

See `docs/engineering/decisions/settlement-currency.md`. Summary: store
currency on the order rather than in a per-partner table, because currency is
a property of the agreement in force when the order was placed, not of the
partner today.

## Failure, security, and recovery

An incorrect backfill or a missing currency on an order would misstate
settlement amounts in reporting. Backfilling all historic rows to USD is safe
because every order placed so far was under a USD agreement. Rollback is
reverting the schema column and adapter/reporting changes; no destructive
migration is involved since the column addition is additive with a default.

## Verification evidence

Unit suite (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`) passed on 2026-07-26
against the current tree; it does not yet cover currency handling since steps
3-5 are not implemented in code.

## Known limits and learning gaps

The plan (`plans/settlement-currency.md`) lists steps 1 and 3 as "in
progress," but only step 1 (schema column) has a change in the working tree;
step 3 (adapter payload) has not been implemented yet. Steps 2 (backfill), 4
(reporting read), and 5 (remove hard-coded currency) are not started. The
reporting read path referenced in the proposal has not been located in this
repository yet.

## References

- Proposal: `docs/proposals/settlement-currency.md`
- Plan: `plans/settlement-currency.md`
- ADR: `docs/engineering/decisions/settlement-currency.md`

# 2026-07-26 · Settlement currency

Change ID: `settlement-currency`
Created: `2026-07-26T13:38:43+00:00`
Status: Accepted

## Context

The settlement currency is currently implied by the partner and hard-coded at
the reporting layer. That is already wrong for one existing partner and two
more partners onboarding this quarter settle in non-USD currencies.

## Options considered

1. Keep deriving currency from the partner at the reporting layer (status
   quo).
2. Add a per-partner currency lookup table.
3. Store the settlement currency on the order row.

## Decision

Choose option 3. Currency is a property of the agreement in force when the
order was placed, not of the partner today; a per-partner table (option 2)
loses that once an agreement changes, and the status quo (option 1) is
already producing wrong reports.

## Consequences and reversal

The adapter and reporting path both take a dependency on the order row
carrying a correct `settlement_currency`. Historic rows are backfilled to
USD. Reversal is dropping the column and reverting the adapter/reporting
reads; this is safe only as long as no order has been placed with a non-USD
currency that reporting has come to depend on.

## Implementation references

- `src/db/schema.py`
- `src/api/partner_adapter.py`
- Reporting read path (not yet located in this repository)

## Supersession

Supersedes: None
Superseded by: None
